races.name: William Hill Epic Boost Fillies' Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Forest Berry
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's filly has won twice over this exact trip and course profile, including a most recent win at Goodwood, and arrives just 12 days fresh — hg:h suggests hood retained, and her ability to front-run cleanly here is the central question for the whole race; note the STYLE_FIT flag is minor given this is the one position she is genuinely competing for.
runners_data.comment: Forest Berry arrives here in the form of her life, winning her last two starts, and with her trainer firing at 35% over the past fortnight, conditions look ideal; she has run over today's trip and going before, and carrying 137 lb from stall 8, she is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Woodhay Wayfarer
runners_data.note: Stepped back up to a mile after a solitary win at Goodwood over this trip, Billy Loughnane takes over from a yard running at 2/16 in the past fortnight; prominent by style and likely to try to tuck in behind Forest Berry, though his only Standard-going win came over this exact trip which is a positive.
runners_data.comment: Woodhay Wayfarer comes into this on the back of a win last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, but two fifth-place finishes before that win and a rating of 74 suggest she faces a stiff test against stronger rivals here.

runners_data.name: Greek Symphony
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's filly has a beautifully consistent recent form string of 3-2-1-3-3 and won over 7f on Standard ground last time, stepping up in trip here for the first time; Mason Paetel claims 3lb and she looks well placed to race prominently and deliver a sustained late challenge.
runners_data.comment: Greek Symphony shaped as a serious threat here, third last time out and a winner three starts back, returning on a quick 22-day turnaround with distance experience and a lively rating edge over her mark; the weight burden of 133 lb is the one factor to overcome.

runners_data.name: Pequenita
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly holds genuine placed form over both today's trip (2nd, 1m, Standard) and 7f at Goodwood, and Oisin Murphy's presence dramatically upgrades her chance of actually securing a forward position despite the congested prominent group — though she is a true prominent type who may find herself further back than ideal given the number of pace horses in this field.
runners_data.comment: Pequenita has shown consistent placing form, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before; yet to score in her last three starts and a middle-of-the-road ranking here suggest she faces a stiff task at the weights with 131 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Crazy Cubana
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 6f at Goodwood before a blip and a modest run at 7f on Standard — Pat Cosgrave rides and she clearly possesses early pace, but with several prominent types ahead of her in the pecking order she is likely to be racing further back than her natural style demands, which compromises her chance in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Crazy Cubana brings solid recent form into this, her third placing two starts back a clear sign of ability, with a win four starts back underlining her class; the worry is that unplaced effort last time out leaves fitness on a retrieval mission after 37 days away.

runners_data.name: Magnesium
runners_data.note: John Butler's filly won over 6f on Standard going but has looked one-paced since, and 42 days off is a notable absence; Rossa Ryan takes the ride and she holds the best credentials among the hold-up runners, but this trip in a slowly-run race is unlikely to produce the late surge she needs.
runners_data.comment: Magnesium has going experience to call on and a win three starts back to advertise her claims, with our rating of 80 putting her among the principals. The risk is two unplaced efforts since that victory suggest she needs to rediscover that form.

runners_data.name: Attack Attack
runners_data.note: George Scott's filly is stepping up in distance for the first time after placing at 7f at Goodwood, wearing blinkers (hg:b), and Liam Wright claims 3lb; a genuine hold-up type who needs the pace to be genuine to utilise her late run, and this race shape makes that a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Attack Attack faces a stiff task here; the 44-day absence is a concern, though a third two starts back offers a slender crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Golden Oasis
runners_data.note: Robert Edwards has a single run in the past 14 days from his yard, and Golden Oasis returns just 10 days after an unseated-rider incident which introduces a significant unknown about her mental state; a true prominent type who won over 7f at Goodwood, she is likely to find herself racing out of position given the volume of pace horses ahead of her, making assessment of her chance difficult.
runners_data.comment: Golden Oasis unseated last time out and, ranked bottom of the field on our figures, is hard to fancy here despite a win two starts back and experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Forest Berry is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to press her hard from the outset, she should be able to dictate a controlled, measured gallop over this flat Kempton mile on Standard to Slow ground. Woodhay Wayfarer and Greek Symphony are also prominent types who will look to track close, but neither has the profile to force a contested pace duel with Forest Berry, meaning the tempo is likely to be honest rather than brutal. Pequenita, Crazy Cubana, and Golden Oasis are all natural prominent racers who cannot all secure their preferred position — of the three, Oisin Murphy on Pequenita gives that runner the best chance of actually slotting into a forward berth, with Crazy Cubana and Golden Oasis most likely to be shuffled back against their will. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable gallop — strongly favours prominent-to-midfield chasers who can travel within striking distance and pounce in the straight, rather than deep hold-up horses who will face a wall of horses to navigate on a track that does not always reward late closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Forest Berry Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Forest Berry is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and control the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Forest Berry dictates from the front at a pace that suits her, never getting into trouble, and delivers a sustained gallop that she is well equipped to maintain having won over this trip and distance style before; the runners tracking her — Greek Symphony and Woodhay Wayfarer — are the primary beneficiaries if she ties up, but she herself is a genuine winning threat if the pace is moderate enough.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just steady enough that the horses tracking Forest Berry in second and third wheel past her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Greek Symphony and Woodhay Wayfarer, positioned close throughout, produce their finishing efforts as Forest Berry's lead narrows, with Greek Symphony's consistent placed form and course suitability making her the most dangerous of the pair; this outcome benefits horses who travel well in a rhythm and do not need pace to be injected late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out and create a clear lane for a hold-up horse to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Magnesium or Attack Attack, sitting last and second last respectively, would need the race to develop into something more genuinely run than this pace map suggests — on Standard to Slow ground at Kempton they would need a wall of tiring horses to navigate through; this is the least natural outcome given the single front-runner and slow ground combination, but Magnesium's win at this trip and going type gives her the best credentials among the hold-up types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Forest Berry goes too fast early for the conditions and blows up, handing the race to whichever horse has settled best.
scenarios.body: Standard to Slow ground at Kempton can catch horses who have over-exerted, and if Forest Berry's energy expenditure early proves excessive the field effectively concertinas in the straight; Greek Symphony, with her strong recent placed form and consistency, or Pequenita, who managed to get a prominent position with Murphy in the saddle, would be the chief beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Forest Berry's ability to get away cleanly and control her own tempo without being pestered is the single biggest variable — if she is harried early by Woodhay Wayfarer or Greek Symphony, the whole race shape shifts.
Golden Oasis unseated last time out (10 days ago) — watch her in the parade ring and early in the race for any signs of unsettled behaviour that could compromise her or disrupt those around her.

Crazy Cubana and Pequenita are both natural front-runners likely to be denied their ground — watch how Pat Cosgrave and Oisin Murphy react to a congested early break, as either could be shuffled wider or back and forced to race very differently to their preferred style.

Standard to Slow ground at Kempton on the AW tends to blunt finishing kicks — horses who race prominently and travel within themselves are historically better placed than deep closers, which makes the confirmed top half of the field more relevant than Magnesium or Attack Attack.

Mason Paetel's 3lb claim on Greek Symphony is worth noting in a field where the top weights are carrying 134-137lbs — the weight relief for a filly with consistent placed form in similar conditions gives her a small but genuine edge in a competitive nursery handicap.

races.name: William Hill London Mile Series Final Handicap Stakes (Series Final - Qualified Horses Only)

runners_data.name: Two Tempting
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and expected to control fractions from the gate; seven-year-old in decent form with strong sim-going data at this trip, though the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild concern if anything forces a different role — his race is likely to be run at his own pace regardless.
runners_data.comment: Two Tempting arrives in fine fettle just 14 days since his last start, has experience of today's trip and conditions, and our rating just edges him to the head of this field — the risk is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Popmaster
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent racer who has solid Kempton form but tends to find one or two too good at the business end; Billy Loughnane takes over and will need a clean break to avoid being shuffled back among the prominent traffic.
runners_data.comment: Popmaster has shown consistent ability in recent starts, finishing fourth twice and fourth again three runs back, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; drawn 13 and carrying 136 lb, he has the profile to outrun his official mark of 96, though he remains yet to score in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Supido
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist stepping back to a mile after a win over this trip in June; Rowan Scott rides for Ian Williams and the Standard to Slow surface is a question mark given just three runs on similar going produced no wins or places.
runners_data.comment: Supido arrives here on a sound fitness pitch after 27 days off, has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 98 gives him a realistic shot from stall 10 off 134 lb; the main concern is that he has been unplaced on his latest start.

runners_data.name: Nikovo
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form with back-to-back thirds and a win over seven furlongs, Oisin Murphy a significant positive booking; hold-up style means he needs a strong enough pace to close into, which hinges on Two Tempting's fractions being honest.
runners_data.comment: Nikovo won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, so there are clear positives, though he carries 132 lb and his rating of 95 ranks him fifth of fourteen, suggesting he faces a stiff enough task against the principals.

runners_data.name: Cavolo Nero
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old in sparkling form — two wins from last three including a course win — and the Standard surface suits given five runs on comparable going yielding two wins and five places; Kaiya Fraser retains the ride and the prominent style is ideally placed for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Cavolo Nero arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has experience of both today's trip and going, making him a compelling threat here; the danger is that 132 lb is a stiff burden to carry.

runners_data.name: The Liffey
runners_data.note: Tremendous record of four wins and four places from eight starts on Standard-equivalent going, and Rossa Ryan is an excellent pilot; holds up but is versatile enough to sit closer, making her dangerous if the tempo creates a seam late — tongue tie and breast girth noted.
runners_data.comment: A winner four times in his last six starts with a runner-up effort last time out, The Liffey arrives here 38 days fresh and has experience of today's trip and going; however, his speed rating of 78 and ranking of seventh in a 14-runner field suggest he faces a stiff ask at the weights with 131 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Percy's Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a win and a place at this course and distance in similar going; headgear (p) worn and the eight-year-old is reliable in handicaps though the trainer's recent form (0/4 T14) is modest — likely to find the prominent positions crowded early.
runners_data.comment: Percy's Lad won two starts back but was fifth last time out, and while he has run over today's trip and going before, a mark of 89 and 129 lb from stall 2 make life no easier for a gelding whose recent form has been inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Dingle
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in reality, though mapped to midfield here given the volume of rear runners; Callum Rodriguez takes over after 72 days off and recent form reads 173000 — the layoff and out-of-role position combine to make this a speculative proposition.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Dingle has been unplaced in his last three starts and a winner six starts back, with 72 days off the track adding to the concerns; experience over today's trip and going is at least something to cling to.

runners_data.name: I'm Workin On It
runners_data.note: Four-year-old prominent type with exceptional sim-going figures (13/15 entries) including four wins; 68 days since last run is worth noting for freshness, but George Wood has ridden him before and the headgear (p) is retained — big each-way profile if securing a clean berth.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 14 on our figures and fourth last time out after 68 days off, I'm Workin On It is hard to fancy at the weights off 126 lb; his one win in recent starts came four starts back, with only a second three starts back to add since.

runners_data.name: Exposure
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner shifted into a midfield map position because there are simply too many horses wanting the same real estate early; Benoit de la Sayette rides for Gosden and the form figures of 5-7434 are modest — the STYLE_FIT and out-of-role tags both temper expectations meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Exposure does at least bring distance experience and a lively fitness edge at 17 days since his latest run, where he finished third two starts back; a rating of 90 gives him fair claims, though consistency remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Warrior Mode
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's four-year-old showed a smart win at this trip on Standard ground recently and Dylan Hogan takes the ride; prominent style is well-suited to this race shape and the horse's last two starts (3rd, 1st) suggest it is in the right order.
runners_data.comment: Warrior Mode won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, with a trainer firing at 35% in the last fortnight; however, he has been unplaced in one of his last five starts and his speed rating of 77 gives pause for thought.

runners_data.name: Blue Prince
runners_data.note: A front-end type by nature who will find himself unable to express that style in a field this congested — Pat Cosgrave is an astute rider and may settle for a mid-division berth, but four-from-seven on Good or AW going without a win on Standard specifically is a flag.
runners_data.comment: Blue Prince won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, but that seventh last time out is a concern, and he carries 124 lb from stall 14 with our rating suggesting he holds a slight edge over his official mark.

runners_data.name: Victory Ace
runners_data.note: Three-year-old on a hat-trick of wins at this trip on Standard going, form reading 265111 — the progression is striking and Finley Marsh has ridden him in recent victories; hold-up style means he needs the pace to be genuine but his sim-going record (8/10, four wins) is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Victory Ace ranks last on our figures and his speed rating leaves him with plenty to find against these rivals, making him hard to fancy on ratings alone; that said, he has winning form in his last three starts and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Vincent Rocks
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse mapped to midfield here due to the volume of rear-runners; Warren Fentiman (3lb claim) takes the ride for Ruth Carr whose T14 figures are thin (1/25), and the visor is worn — recent form of -03025 does not inspire confidence at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, Vincent Rocks faces a stiff task, and a trainer striking at just 4% in the past fortnight does little to encourage; experience over today's trip and going, plus a second two starts back, offer slim comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Two Tempting is the sole confirmed front-runner and, racing at Kempton over a mile on Standard to Slow ground, will look to dictate from the off at a controlled, measured tempo — Jonathan Portman's seven-year-old has the race-craft to set fractions that suit himself rather than the field. Behind him, Popmaster, Cavolo Nero, Percy's Lad, Warrior Mode and I'm Workin On It are all genuine prominent types, but this field holds more pace-hungry horses than can realistically secure their favoured position — Two Tempting will take the rail, Cavolo Nero (in excellent form) and Warrior Mode are likeliest to slot in directly behind, while Popmaster and Percy's Lad will be squeezed wider or further back than ideal. With only one horse genuinely setting the fractions at a sustainable clip and the Standard to Slow surface blunting any late surge, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel close to the pace without being the one doing the work — prominent types who get a clean position in second or third are the profile to side with, ahead of hold-up horses who will find the tempo insufficient to create the gaps they need late on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Position Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tempting controls the front at a fair but unhurried tempo and the prominent brigade settles cleanly in behind.
scenarios.body: Cavolo Nero and Warrior Mode, both in fine fettle and comfortable at this trip on this surface, are best placed to travel on the bridle and pounce inside the final furlong without needing a scorching pace injection; the Standard to Slow surface rewards horses that sustain rather than accelerate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tempting sets a genuinely strong pace and the prominent pack press on, stretching the race and opening a late lane.
scenarios.body: Nikovo and The Liffey, both proven at this track and distance and carrying excellent recent form, have the finishing kick to mow through a tiring field if the tempo is honest enough; Oisin Murphy on Nikovo in particular would be drawn into his ideal scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tempting — though tagged as racing slightly out of role — dictates an unchallenged, slow-burn tempo and the field fails to organise a coherent challenge.
scenarios.body: On a Standard to Slow surface with no horse willing to press early and a large, 14-runner field creating traffic issues, Two Tempting could simply coast to the line having never been headed; Portman's horse does have strong sim-going form at this course and trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position among the prominent contingent causes bunching, interference and a muddling early sectional.
scenarios.body: Blue Prince and Exposure, both natural prominent types forced into unfamiliar midfield positions, could find pockets opening unexpectedly if the race breaks up; however, because both are racing out of their natural role this scenario is the least reliable to predict and the least likely to deliver for them.

watchPoints.text: Cavolo Nero is on a hat-trick of near-wins or wins and sits perfectly placed stylistically — watch whether Kaiya Fraser secures a clean run in second or third as early as the two-furlong pole, as any traffic at a crucial moment would be costly.

Victory Ace has won three consecutive miles on this surface and is the most in-form horse in the field on a form-line basis — watch whether the hold-up position and Standard to Slow conditions allow him to unleash his finishing effort before the line arrives.

The prominent pack of Popmaster, Percy's Lad, I'm Workin On It and Blue Prince will all attempt to press Two Tempting early; watch the first two furlongs for crowding and shuffling that could unsettle one or more of them and scramble the race shape entirely.

Nikovo with Oisin Murphy aboard is a live danger only if the pace is brisk enough — watch Two Tempting's early fractions because a dawdling tempo renders the hold-up brigade near-irrelevant on this surface.

Dingle (72 days off) and Vincent Rocks (visor, modest recent form) both carry question marks around readiness or suitability — watch market moves at the off to gauge stable confidence, particularly for Dingle given the Camacho yard's unexplained absence.

races.name: William Hill September Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Dubai Future
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran for Saeed bin Suroor who revels in hold-up tactics and produced a career-best RPR-136 win at Goodwood over 2m last time; the drop back to 1m4f on AW is the key query, but his Polytrack form includes a third at Lingfield and his relentless galloping style suits a slow pace that others underestimate.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, Dubai Future arrives here with mixed recent form but experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; the burden of 136 lb is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Almeric
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old has been a model of consistency at 1m2f–1m4f this season, placing five times in his last six, and Rob Hornby's patient style suits if the race develops steadily; he has yet to win beyond 1m2f on good ground and needs to prove the extra furlong genuinely helps him here.|

runners_data.name: Constitution Hill
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's star hurdler has surprised with two AW wins at Lingfield (1m2f, Standard) but races off a 164-day break and steps up sharply in class; though a genuine front-runner by instinct, he cannot have it all his own way with Gethin in the field and will find himself racing in a position he rarely inhabits — the yard is 0/1 in the last 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 164 days is the obvious concern, and ranked last of six on our figures he faces a stiff task, though back-to-back wins in his last two starts and experience over today's trip and going offer some crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Gethin
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows' lightly-raced four-year-old is the confirmed pace-maker of this contest and is capable of front-running to victory, as demonstrated by his AW win at Kempton over 1m — the step up to 1m4f is the open question, though his 2m2f stamina index is unproven; Callum Rodriguez will likely go easy enough to preserve him.|
runners_data.comment: Gethin shaped with plenty of credit when runner-up two starts back and was a winner three starts back, so the ability is not in question; he acts on today's going, but that 63-day absence is the one factor to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Arras
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up specialist won impressively over 1m2f at Goodwood but was a beaten favourite in his last two starts at longer trips on good ground; Rossa Ryan will sit and wait, and the AW surface may be the freshener he needs, though the concern is whether his finishing kick translates to Polytrack.|
runners_data.comment: Pride Of Arras shaped well last time, finishing second, and returns here 42 days on having run over today's trip before; carrying 133 lb is a stern ask, but his overall profile makes him our preferred pick in this six-runner contest.

runners_data.name: Tornado Alert
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy teams up with this Bin Suroor four-year-old who has won over 1m on soft and 1m on AW (Standard), giving him surface credibility; he will press Gethin from a prominent position but his form over 1m2f–1m4f is modest and a career high at this distance remains unproven.|
runners_data.comment: Tornado Alert won two starts back and was runner-up three starts back, showing consistent front-rank form at this level, and he has experience over today's trip carrying 133 lb; the concern is whether his fourth last time out represents a return to top form.

runners_data.name: Warrant Holder
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's consistent type has won on Kempton AW (1m2f, Standard) and at 1m2f–1m4f on multiple surfaces, giving him strong course credentials; by nature a prominent runner, he will find himself shuffled back by the volume of pace in this field — Benoit de la Sayette will need to manage that displacement carefully, and his 56-day layoff (headgear: tongue-tie) adds a minor unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Warrant Holder has been out of the frame in his most recent start and, ranked fifth of six on our figures, is hard to fancy here, though he does bring distance and going experience to the table and showed a winner's instinct two and three starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Gethin is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to pressure him from the gates, he is highly likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front at Kempton's flat, undemanding 1m4f AW circuit. Tornado Alert and Almeric will track him prominently, but neither has the profile to burn him off early, so the pace is unlikely to be truly testing — a steady-to-moderate tempo is the most probable outcome. This field does contain more prominent-minded horses than the shape can accommodate: Constitution Hill and Warrant Holder are natural front-runners who figure to be shuffled back into unfamiliar midfield berths, and of the genuine prominents, Gethin is best-placed to actually secure his natural position. A controlled pace with Gethin on or near the lead throughout favours hold-up horses who possess a late turn of foot, and at this distance on a surface riding Standard To Slow, those who can sit patiently and deliver a sustained finishing effort into the home straight are structurally advantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gethin Controls, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Gethin dictates a modest pace and the hold-up horses are delivered with a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Gethin sets a comfortable tempo that compresses the field but ultimately sets it up for those coming from off the pace, as the slow-ish gallop means fresher legs behind bloom late into the straight. Dubai Future and Pride Of Arras, both natural hold-up types with course-suitable profiles, are most likely to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Gethin Front-Runs Clean Win
scenarios.trigger: If Gethin's controlled lead proves unassailable and no hold-up horse can generate enough momentum off the steady pace.
scenarios.body: With no rival able to put him under early pressure, Gethin simply conserves energy in front before kicking clear entering the Kempton straight; his one-mile AW form and ability to front-run efficiently is the key asset here. Tornado Alert, tracking closely, could be best of the rest if the pace never truly develops.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duel, Midfield Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Tornado Alert or Almeric apply unexpected early pressure to Gethin and the tempo genuinely lifts.
scenarios.body: A contested lead at a true pace would take edge off the principals and open the race up for a horse sitting just off the action, with Almeric — proven at staying on when the gallop is strong — particularly suited. Constitution Hill, though displaced from his natural position, could also benefit if the field is strung out and gaps appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Redistributed Types Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If Constitution Hill or Warrant Holder push forward early and scramble the expected order.
scenarios.body: Both are natural prominent types forced wide of their preferred spots; if either instinctively contests the pace it could create an untidy race with an uneven tempo that scrambles probability. Warrant Holder's Kempton AW form and fitness edge after 56 days off makes him the more interesting of the two if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Gethin's pace-setting role is entirely uncontested — watch whether Callum Rodriguez elects to stretch the field early or dawdles, as the tempo he sets will define every other horse's chance.

Constitution Hill and Warrant Holder are both instinctive front-runners likely to be squeezed back at the start; if either fights for position against their nature it could create early scrimmaging and unsettle the race shape entirely.

Dubai Future carries 136lbs on OR=113 and is a ten-year-old dropping from 2m — watch how the market reacts to whether punters view the AW trip as a positive or a limitation, as his fitness and Bin Suroor record (1/4 last 14 days) is a concern.

The going is described as Standard To Slow across every race today — not merely Standard — so any horse with a strong preference for a genuine fast surface (particularly those dropping from summer turf form) may find the Kempton AW slower than expected, favouring resolute galloping types.

Pride Of Arras was beaten at 10/12f on good in his last two; watch whether Rossa Ryan elects to switch tactics and ride him more prominently than usual if the pace looks falsely slow, given his one win this season came from off the pace at a genuinely strong gallop.

races.name: William Hill Sirenia Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Adaay of Scarlett
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's consistent front-runner has five consecutive placed efforts at 6f but has not won since May, raising questions about whether a near-peak effort is still forthcoming; races in a hood (headgear noted), 15 days fresh, and must find a clean break to avoid the speed-horse pile-up off the stalls.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and classy, Adaay of Scarlett has finished second on four occasions in recent starts and a winner six starts back, returning here fit on a 15-day turnaround having run over today's trip; the main risk is that fifth last time out suggests he may just find one too good again.

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's colt has winning form on Kempton's equivalent surface (Standard) and brings a 4/28 trainer form angle over 14 days that is solid; prominent from the gates, Finley Marsh will need to thread past the five-horse speed clash early to secure a clear run on the inside turning in.
runners_data.comment: Placed second two starts back and third three starts back, Agamemnon arrives on a sharp 15-day turnaround in solid recent trim, and has run over today's trip before; the fourth last time out is the one form line that gives slight pause.

runners_data.name: Moonrise
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners the Andrew Balding-trained two-year-old who has won twice at 6f including on Standard ground — the most directly relevant surface form in the race; 42 days since last run is the notable flag, though Balding horses frequently return fit and Murphy's tactical intelligence is a premium asset in a congested pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Moonrise arrives on the back of a win last time out, with another victory three starts back and experience over today's trip and going — a compelling profile. The main risk is the 42-day absence at 129 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Social Symbol
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's runner won over 5f on Good ground but has been beaten on each of his last three outings, including twice at 6f; drops to OR 96 and while the yard's 1/21 14-day strike rate is lean, Rob Hornby gives him an honest platform if he can slot into the first three off the break.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner four starts back, Social Symbol arrives here in good heart after 28 days off, has run over today's trip, and his 102 rating makes him an appealing pick to go one better from stall 7 carrying 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Tawakal
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unexposed — just two starts — with a win at 6f on Good and a runner-up at the same trip; Jack Mitchell partners for the Crisfords and the horse's prominent style should allow a trouble-free passage if the chaos ahead of him is managed cleanly, making him an interesting each-way proposition on the upgraded standard.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures, Tawakal faces a stiff ask under 129 lb from stall 1, though he has run over today's trip and arrives on the back of a win and a runner-up finish in his last two starts.

runners_data.name: Bated Benevolence
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's filly won over 6f on Standard at Kempton most recently — the most precise surface and course match in the field — and returns quickly at 14 days on a 4/15 trainer hot streak; despite wanting to lead, that specific course-and-going win gives her a legitimate pace-survival angle if she can bounce out cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Bated Benevolence faces a stiff ask, though she arrives on a sound note — a runner-up last time out and a winner two starts back — and has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Efsixteen
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie (headgear noted) for George Scott, having won over 5f at Goodwood last time; stepping up to 6f for only the second time and moving to a synthetic surface, both factors introducing unknowns that temper confidence despite the evident raw ability in a debut win.
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back but only fourth on her most recent outing, Efsixteen returns after 22 days and has run over today's trip before; the 126 lb burden and a ranking of sixth of nine in our ratings are the checks on her claims.

runners_data.name: Evenfall
runners_data.note: George Boughey's unbeaten two-year-old (wins at 6f Good and 5f Good) is a genuine prominent racer by style — the mapping to a hold-up position reflects field redistribution rather than how Loughnane will deploy him; a STYLE_FIT tag of 0.80 applies, so discount his chance in shapes that require a true closing kick, though his raw form is unquestionable.

runners_data.name: Nicely
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's colt won over 6f on Soft last time and has front-running form going back two wins; Rowan Scott rides and 14 days since last run is tight but the horse has been busy, and if he breaks fastest of the speed horses his experience leading over the trip gives him a genuine each-way chance of lasting.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures despite an official mark of 89, Nicely has won twice in her last four starts and returns on a quick turnaround from stall two, with experience over today's trip adding mild encouragement, but the speed rating of 79 leaves her hard to fancy at this level.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sun
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's colt — trainer 0/14 over 14 days is a stark cold-stable flag — ran poorly last two (14th and 20th) after a promising 2nd, though the drop back to 5f wins on Good suggests the current 6f trip may be at the limit; Daniel Muscutt will look to track the chaos and pounce, but confidence is tempered by recent form and the trainer's current run.
runners_data.comment: Shimmering Sun returns after 16 days carrying 126 lb from stall 6, and has run over today's trip before. A winner four starts back, she was second two starts back, but has disappointed on her most recent outing, leaving her profile a touch mixed.

races.paceDynamic: Adaay of Scarlett, Social Symbol, Bated Benevolence, Efsixteen, and Nicely all want to lead, creating near-certain early carnage over Kempton's sharp 6f on a Standard to Slow surface — the tempo will be fierce from the gates and the pace will only relent once the field turns into the straight. That congestion between four or five speed horses for three or four positions in the first furlong raises real traffic danger approaching the two-furlong pole, with elbows likely thrown heading into the bend. Evenfall is tagged as a redistributed runner — a genuine prominent type pushed back on paper because the early positions are already oversubscribed; of the true front-runners, Adaay of Scarlett and Nicely hold the clearest claims to actually secure a forward berth given their tactical speed and recent lead-dictating form. This shape — a hot early gallop that tests stamina and strings the field out — heavily favours horses with a prominent-but-controlled style who can slot just off the speed and unleash a sustained finish: Agamemnon, Moonrise, and Shimmering Sun fit that profile best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the five speed horses burn each other off and a smooth-travelling prominent runner lands in the perfect stalking position rounding the final bend.
scenarios.body: The early leaders bleed each other dry, leaving the winner to cruise into the slipstream before hitting the front at the furlong pole with a clear run; this shape suits horses who can race handily without fighting for position in the melee.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives Blitz
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner breaks sharply enough to establish a clear lead and control the tempo at a fraction below suicidal pace.
scenarios.body: One pacemaker — most likely Adaay of Scarlett or Nicely — carves out a small advantage early and, crucially, is not harried every step, conserving just enough to repel challengers late; Standard to Slow conditions reward the horse who sets an honest but not ruinous gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners collectively set a truly suicidal pace that sees every prominent challenger also emptying out, creating a gap for a hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: The entire front half of the field ties up inside the final furlong, and a horse with a genuine late kick can pick them off; however, because Evenfall — the nominal hold-up representative — is a natural prominent racer who has been redistributed, this scenario is structurally weakened by the absence of an authentic closing type.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the traffic danger two-to-three out causes interference or checks across several prominent contenders, gifting the race to whoever escapes cleanest.
scenarios.body: A scrimmage on the bend bunches the field and delivers the race to opportunists who find daylight first rather than to the best horse; pace scenarios collapse into a sprint for the line among whichever runners avoided trouble.

watchPoints.text: Adaay of Scarlett and Nicely are on a collision course for the same early position — watch for bumping or checking inside the first two furlongs as five speed horses compress into three berths off the stalls.

Evenfall is a natural prominent racer mapped to hold-up on paper; Billy Loughnane is likely to push forward regardless, tightening the speed pocket further and increasing the risk of interference approaching the bend.
Moonrise is 42 days since her last run — monitor the paddock for any signs of a below-par coat or unsettled behaviour, as a ring-rusty display at this level would be quickly punished.

Shimmering Sun's trainer Harry Eustace is 0/14 over the last 14 days — a significant cold-barn signal in a Group 3 that demands peak preparation; expect the market to reflect this if money fails to flow at the off.

Standard to Slow conditions at Kempton AW will blunt finishing kicks and reward horses that conserve energy early — any runner caught in the first-furlong scramble for position will pay a steep price in the closing stages.

races.name: William Hill Price Boosts Every Day Fillies' Handicap Stakes (London Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Zighy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won on this exact course and surface (Standard) on most recent start 15 days ago, trained by in-form George Boughey; the hg:p headgear suggests she settles well up with the pace and her sim-going record of 3 wins from 10 is solid — well placed to capitalise if the front-runners battle each other into submission.
runners_data.comment: Zighy arrives in sound nick after a third last time out, and a winner five starts back, with experience over today's trip in her favour; 135 lb and a trainer firing at just 4% in the past fortnight are the checks against her here.

runners_data.name: Lady Roxby
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly returning after 43 days off for Michael Herrington, whose yard is striking at a modest 3/13 strike rate in the past 14 days; sim-going record is a very weak 0 wins from 15 on similar surfaces and her last-five finishes are dominated by 7th-place efforts — needs everything to go right from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Rated marginally top of these on our figures, Lady Roxby has run over today's trip and going before and draws stall two carrying 135 lb; the concern is a string of sevenths and a ninth in her last four starts leaves her yet to win in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Powdering
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type who won on Good ground most recently but holds no wins on Standard/similar surfaces from 15 attempts; trainer Herrington's double-runner angle is interesting, but Seamus Cronin's 5lb claim could help offset the weight, and her last run produced only a 7th — needs the pace to be truly scorching.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner three starts ago, Powdering arrives in decent recent form, though she was well beaten last time out; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 135 lb from stall one, and her rating of 83 offers mild encouragement.

runners_data.name: Tarot
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed front-runners and will fight Veil Of Clouds for the early lead, which is her chief danger; Roger Varian's filly has a 1W2P record in sim-going from 7 runs but the hg:h headgear indicates she can be headstrong — 36 days since last run and facing another front-runner could see her energy dissipated before the business end.
runners_data.comment: Tarot won four starts back and her rating of 87 marks her out as a strong player in this field, with experience over today's trip and going adding to her claims from draw 11; the worry is that she has finished sixth, sixth and seventh in her last three starts.

runners_data.name: Eskimo Pie
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly from Jane Chapple-Hyam, whose yard has had no winners from 11 starts in the past 14 days; won at 6f on Good ground and has some Standard form, but has drifted in trip of late — Daniel Muscutt takes the ride and she is one of the more honest hold-up types genuinely capable of late progress if the pace is fierce.
runners_data.comment: Eskimo Pie catches the eye on the back of a win last time out, and at 24 days between runs she arrives fresh and ready to go. She has experience of today's distance and going, and 134 lb from stall 10 looks workable for a filly this in-form.

runners_data.name: Shallow
runners_data.note: A true hold-up/wait-and-weave type whose natural position is further back than the map shows, displaced to midfield due to runner volume; best form shows a habit of running places (multiple seconds) rather than winning, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence — hg:v visor may sharpen focus, but racing out of role reduces the scenario value here.
runners_data.comment: Shallow has finished second three times in her last six starts and returns in good order just 15 days after her latest runner-up effort, carrying 134 lb from stall 8 with experience of today's trip and conditions; the main risk is that she remains winless in recent starts and will need to finally convert.

runners_data.name: Paradise Walk
runners_data.note: Prominent filly from Ralph Beckett, whose yard is firing at 9/45 in the past 14 days; has two wins from eight prominent-style runs on similar going and the hg:b blinkers suggest she is kept sharp — 39 days since her last run is worth monitoring but her form figures include two recent wins at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Two consecutive wins three and four starts back give Paradise Walk some credibility, but she has been unplaced on her latest outing and, ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, the weight of evidence makes her hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Veil Of Clouds
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner and arguably the more course-savvy of the two, with four starts on Standard Polytrack including one win and three places from five sim-going runs — Oisin Murphy's booking is significant and the hg:t hood keeps her settled; whether she can dominate depends entirely on Tarot's early willingness to press her.
runners_data.comment: Veil Of Clouds won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but she carries 131 lb from stall four and her trainer has struck at just five per cent in the past fortnight, which tempers enthusiasm despite that recent victory.

runners_data.name: Calling A Star
runners_data.note: Prominent type with two wins on Standard ground and a credible 3/10 sim-going record; Richard Hughes's yard is active at 4/28 recently, and Finley Marsh takes the ride — 38 days away from the track is a minor concern but her 6f course form is sound and she could be ideally positioned just off the contested pace.
runners_data.comment: Calling A Star won three starts back but has since been out of the money, including an unplaced effort last time; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 131 lb from stall seven, and returns after 38 days off.

runners_data.name: Lope El Fuego
runners_data.note: Prominent filly who has not won beyond 6f on Good ground and whose last two runs were 9ths; 58 days since last run is the longest break in the field and Warren Greatrex's yard is only 3/11 recently — needs to show she retains her form and the extended absence is a meaningful flag against.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive ninth-place finishes in her last two starts make Lope El Fuego difficult to fancy, ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, and 58 days off the track adds further uncertainty; she has run over today's trip and that third a few starts back hints at residual ability.

runners_data.name: Rumble Ruby
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by nature, but displaced to midfield on the map because there are simply too many prominent types in this field to accommodate her naturally; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim could help her get closer than expected, and her sim-going form shows consistency at 6f on Standard, but the STYLE_FIT flag means she is unlikely to get the race run to suit her position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying 129 lb, Rumble Ruby faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive third last time out, has run over today's trip, and her two wins in recent starts show she knows how to find the line.

races.paceDynamic: Tarot and Veil Of Clouds are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 6f on Standard to Slow Polytrack at Kempton, creating an honest, pressured gallop rather than a soft, uncontested lead for either. With Zighy and Paradise Walk also wanting to race prominently, the early sections will be genuinely contested, ensuring the pace is maintained throughout and the race will be run at a true tempo. This shape — a fought-over lead on a surface playing Standard to Slow — historically compresses finishing positions and gives a significant edge to prominent-to-midfield horses with the tactical speed to sit just off the pace and produce a sustained late effort, rather than pure front-runners who will have burned energy fighting for position. The field carries more prominent and front-running types than can all be accommodated near the speed, and of the redistributed horses, Rumble Ruby and Shallow are both genuine in their natural roles but are unlikely to secure their preferred positions — Tarot, Veil Of Clouds, and Zighy are most likely to actually hold the front spots from the break.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Tarot and Veil Of Clouds fight for the front and the pace is strong enough to expose those who over-commit early.
scenarios.body: The two genuine front-runners battle throughout, leaving them vulnerable inside the final furlong, and a well-positioned prominent horse who has tracked the pace comfortably storms through. Zighy and Paradise Walk are ideally placed to capitalise, both comfortable racing prominently at this course and trip with proven Standard going form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two leaders — most likely Veil Of Clouds — manages to slip the field fractionally and convert raw pace into a winning advantage.
scenarios.body: Veil Of Clouds has strong course-and-distance form in similar conditions, top jockey booking in Oisin Murphy, and could dictate if Tarot fails to match her stride for stride early. A horse with her natural rhythm and tactical sense under Murphy could steal a march on the pack and the Standard to Slow surface may blunt the closers' finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Picks Up
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly fierce and the front-runners tie each other up, leaving the race to those tracking in mid-division.
scenarios.body: Eskimo Pie and Calling A Star, capable of sitting a few lengths off the speed, would benefit from a rapid early tempo that burns out the leaders before the two-furlong marker. Calling A Star's two wins on Standard ground and Eskimo Pie's course form make them the most credible beneficiaries of this shape if the pace truly roasts the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Closes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or fractional splits are extreme enough to allow genuine hold-up horses to motor home from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Lady Roxby and Powdering are the truest hold-up types in the field, though both have struggled to convert their running style into wins, and the Standard to Slow surface at Kempton typically rewards those closer to the pace rather than back-markers. This scenario is materially discounted because several horses tagged in the hold-up zone are redistributed types — the true closers lack the consistent finishing form to make this a high-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Tarot and Veil Of Clouds will lock horns from the first stride — watch for either to be shuffled sideways at the break or to over-race in the early duel, which could see both emptying before the two-furlong pole and handing the race to the chasers.

Rumble Ruby and Shallow are both operating out of their natural positions due to field congestion — if either is forced wider or loses ground at the start trying to find their preferred spot, their chance will be materially compromised before the race has properly begun.

Lope El Fuego returns after 58 days without a run — the longest absence in the field — and her last two efforts were distant 9ths; watch for signs of a need-the-run display that would make her irrelevant to the result.

The going is confirmed Standard to Slow for this race, not the Standard listed in the race conditions — this slower surface tends to blunt pure pace advantages and can bring hold-up horses closer to the front-runners in the final furlong, mildly improving Lady Roxby and Eskimo Pie's theoretical chances.

Paradise Walk wears blinkers (hg:b) and is dropping down from a 17th-place effort at Goodwood on her most recent seasonal start, but her prior two runs produced wins and Beckett's yard is in strong form — watch her position at the two-furlong pole as an indicator of whether the blinkers have sharpened her response.

races.name: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Haku
runners_data.note: Strong course and similar-going profile (13 of 15 runs on AW/Standard, four wins) and arrives fresh on just seven days' rest; natural hold-up horse who will need a strong pace to close into, which this race is unlikely to provide, so his chance hinges on a sprint-finish developing.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner five starts back, Haku has solid recent form to build on, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; at 135 lb, the weight is the one factor to overcome.

runners_data.name: Astro King
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type whose sole similar-going run produced a zero finish; the step from 10-11f up to 1m4f is a positive, but his recent form string of blanks and the near-absence of AW form makes him a speculative entry at best.
runners_data.comment: Astro King heads this 11-runner field on ratings and shaped with fair merit when fourth last time out, though he remains winless in recent starts; back within a workable 16 days and carrying 135 lb over a trip he has tackled before, he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: King's Code
runners_data.note: Prominent racer fitted with a visor, returning after 23 days for the in-form David Evans yard which has two wins from 19 recent runners; two wins from 15 similar-going runs and a course win at 10f suggest the step to 1m4f needs proving, but he is well-placed to track Topteam throughout.
runners_data.comment: King's Code won three starts back and returns on a handy 23-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions and a rating of 97 putting him firmly among the dangers; the worry is two consecutive eighths since that victory.

runners_data.name: Whitcombe Rockstar
runners_data.note: Lightly raced prominent type returning from 72 days off, but the form is compelling — two wins and a second from her last four starts over similar tracks and surfaces, including a course-and-distance win; Josephine Gordon gets the call for Kieran Burke's yard and this horse's record of striking from just off the pace makes her the chief danger to Topteam.
runners_data.comment: Whitcombe Rockstar won back-to-back races earlier in this sequence and ran a solid second three starts back, giving him a strong recent profile, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is 72 days off the track without a run since.

runners_data.name: Topteam
runners_data.note: Confirmed sole front-runner, ridden by Oisin Murphy for Balding's yard which is in fine nick (9 wins from 55 in 14 days); returning from 98 days off is worth monitoring, but his 1m4f win on Standard AW and the certainty of uncontested lead make him the axis around which this entire race revolves.
runners_data.comment: Topteam was second two starts back and got off the mark four starts back, so the ability is there, but he comes into this unplaced last time and a lengthy 98-day absence to overcome, making him a fascinating if uncertain each-way proposition at a hefty 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Incensed
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best effort in similar going was a runner-up finish over 1m4f on Standard AW — the one occasion the conditions truly matched today's; six weeks since last run and a trainer with no runners in 14 days suggests this is a quiet prep, yet the distance profile is right if a strong pace develops.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Incensed does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and her rating of 96 suggests more ability than her official mark of 89 implies, but an unplaced effort last time and a fifth before that are a concern at 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Majestic
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old whose true style is hold-up but is mapped to midfield due to the volume of hold-up horses in this field; his one similar-going run produced no better than a place, and while he has course form, the unnatural tracking position will blunt his late finish.
runners_data.comment: Majestic shaped with promise when third last time out and has experience over today's trip, but he has been winless in his last five starts and that unplaced effort two runs back tempers expectations somewhat at a mark of 88.

runners_data.name: Primo Lara
runners_data.note: In-form horse with two recent wins including a Standard AW victory, but his natural hold-up style is compromised here — pushed into a midfield slot he does not naturally inhabit because of the density of closers in this field, meaning he must race against his instincts if he is to recreate recent winning form.
runners_data.comment: Primo Lara won two of his last six starts, including back-to-back victories two and three runs back, but he was beaten into fourth last time out and his speed figure of 79 leaves him needing to find more against stronger company here.

runners_data.name: Tiernan
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old who has shown he can win from hold-up and has a recent runner-up on Good ground, but today he is housed in midfield against his preferred style; Rossa Ryan rides for Iain Jardine's yard that is 3 from 29 over 14 days, suggesting modest momentum.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Tiernan is hard to recommend despite a win two starts back; he was fifth last time out and his speed rating lags his other marks, leaving him a difficult proposition even at a workable weight of 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Elsass
runners_data.note: Has back-to-back wins in his form string and Rob Hornby takes the ride for Charlie Johnston's busy yard (5 from 39 in 14 days), but his best form has come on Good ground and his three Standard/Soft runs have yielded mixed results; like the other redistributed runners, he is racing outside his natural role and that style compromise must temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Seventh in each of his last two starts, Elsass faces a stiff task ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and his two wins in recent starts show he retains ability when conditions click.

runners_data.name: Sudu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old is a prominent type whose sole similar-going run was two from seven on Standard AW; Rowan Scott takes over in the saddle and the step up to 1m4f is unexplored, yet his likely position just behind Topteam gives him tactical prominence that could prove useful if the pace drops.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Sudu has finished sixth and eighth in his last two starts, making him hard to fancy despite a win three starts back and experience over today's trip.

races.paceDynamic: Topteam is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 11-runner field over 1m4f on a Standard to Slow Kempton AW surface, and with no rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, Oisin Murphy can dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the front. Whitcombe Rockstar and King's Code are the only genuine prominent types able to track close, with Sudu likely filling a similar early role, meaning the race will be strung out behind Topteam in an ordered, low-pressure queue. The hold-up brigade — Haku, Astro King, Incensed, Majestic, Primo Lara, Tiernan and Elsass — is substantial, but the field holds far more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, and Majestic, Primo Lara, Tiernan and Elsass are redistributed to midfield, meaning they will not enjoy a genuine tracking role or a true closer's run. The race shape firmly favours prominent horses that can track Topteam's controlled pace and strike turning in, or Topteam itself if the gallop is slow enough to play to a kicker's hand.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Topteam Controls And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Topteam is allowed to dictate a modest, uncontested gallop and Murphy produces him late off a slow burn.
scenarios.body: Topteam sets a relaxed pace with Whitcombe Rockstar and King's Code in attendance, and with nothing to pressure him, he conserves energy before quickening away from the front in the straight; at OR 91 with Balding's in-form yard and a top jockey, this controlled scenario is the most likely race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Whitcombe Rockstar or King's Code track Topteam closely enough to pounce when the pace slows in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Whitcombe Rockstar's in-form profile — two wins and multiple places on similar surfaces — means she is ideally positioned just off Topteam's shoulder to capitalise the moment the gallop lifts; King's Code, fitted with a visor, has course form and David Evans's yard is firing with two wins from 19 recent runners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow, tempting Topteam to dawdle, and a hold-up horse with a strong late kick catches the field flat-footed.
scenarios.body: Haku has the strongest similar-going profile in the field (13 of 15 runs, four wins) and arrives fresh on just seven days' rest having won over this course and distance previously; however, the abundance of hold-up types means traffic and a lack of a genuine test are real risks, and Incensed and Primo Lara also have claims if the straight produces a sprint.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of midfield horses causes interference or the pace is so slow that the field bunches violently in the straight.
scenarios.body: With four hold-up types pushed into midfield against their nature, the straight could see a messy, crowded finish as Majestic, Tiernan and Elsass fail to get clear runs from their unnatural positions; in this scenario a horse with course craft and a clear passage — Whitcombe Rockstar or Haku — benefits most.

watchPoints.text: Topteam's 98-day layoff is the single biggest race-day variable — watch in the paddock and early strides for any sign of ring rustiness, as his ability to travel smoothly from the front underpins the dominant scenario.

Whitcombe Rockstar returns from 72 days off and must be monitored for freshness in the parade ring; if she travels strongly in the early stages tracking Topteam, she becomes the most dangerous horse in the race.

The four redistributed hold-up horses (Majestic, Primo Lara, Tiernan, Elsass) racing in unnatural midfield positions create a compression risk in the home straight — watch for traffic problems and potential interference as they all seek the same passage simultaneously.

King's Code wears a visor today which is new headgear; watch for a positive behavioural response in the early stages, as prominent racers with freshly applied visors can be notably sharper out of the gate.

The Standard to Slow going is slower than many of these horses' form runs on Standard AW — Haku's strong similar-going record is an asset, while Astro King's near-zero AW form is a significant concern on this surface.

races.name: William Hill Keep Your Raceday Positive Handicap Stakes (London Stayers' Series Qualifier) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Naval Tribute
runners_data.note: Won over 16f at Goodwood and 11f at Kempton on Standard, wearing a visor here; the 96-day absence is the main query but James Owen's T14 strike rate of 2/36 suggests caution, and his STYLE_FIT tag confirms he is racing forward of his natural role, though the trip and going suit him well.
runners_data.comment: Naval Tribute arrives on the back of three wins in his last six starts, including a victory last time out, and has experience of both today's trip and going — he's no stranger to these conditions. The main risk is a 96-day absence.

runners_data.name: Barenboim
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up specialist whose recent form figures of 698930 and sim-going record of 10/15 make him hard to fancy; Tom Dascombe has had no winners in the last 14 days and, while the 16f trip is within range, his habit of finishing well back on Standard surfaces is a significant concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts yet a step back to third two runs ago showed residual ability, and Barenboim's experience over today's trip and going, combined with a rating of 85 that tops this six-runner field, makes him the one to side with.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Jack Jones, who has produced two winners in 17 recent runners — a confident booking for a horse whose form string of 1-2222 is almost admirably consistent at 16f on Good; the slight concern is that Standard to Slow Kempton AW is a different test and his sim-going record of 6/15 does not scream suitability.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and lively coming into this, An Bradan Feasa has been runner-up four times in his last five starts, with a win five starts back, and arrives on a sharp 22-day turnaround with distance and going experience in his favour. The main risk is whether he can finally convert his placed efforts into victory.

runners_data.name: Betelgeuse
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old whose genuine home is at the back of the field — placed here at midfield on the map because of the field's hold-up-heavy composition — but trainer S Woods has two winners from eight recent runners and the horse's pattern of 2s and 3s over staying trips shows consistent resolution at the finish.
runners_data.comment: Betelgeuse has been winless in his last six starts, and ranked last on our figures he faces a stiff task here, though he returns on a sharp turnaround of 14 days, has run over today's trip, and those placings show he can knuckle down.

runners_data.name: Campeona
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old is the yard's most powerful weapon here, with three wins from her last five and a hat-trick of victories at 16f and 17f suggesting she is still progressing up the staying ladder; the sim-going entry of 3/8 on comparable surfaces is thin but the Prescott operation typically targets these London Stayers' Series qualifiers with intent.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures and carrying 126 lb, Campeona looks to have plenty to find on ratings despite a lively recent sequence that includes three wins in her last five starts; she has run over today's trip and going, and her trainer is striking at 35% in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Flash Kozo
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on Standard going and placed twice more at staying trips, so the step to 2m asks a genuine stamina question on debut at the trip; Harry Eustace has had no winners in 14 days, and as a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the map, Flash Kozo's chance depends heavily on a searching gallop materialising that simply may not arrive with Naval Tribute in front.
runners_data.comment: Flash Kozo arrives in fine nick — a winner two starts back and second last time out, he handles today's going and comes here fresh off an 18-day break carrying 124 lb, though his speed rating of 65 is the main risk against stronger rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Naval Tribute is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with just six runners over 2m on a Standard to Slow surface, will take them along at a pace entirely of his own choosing — Rossa Ryan can dictate from the front without any genuine pressure from the field. An Bradan Feasa is the only other prominent-style runner but is more of a tracking type than a leader, so Naval Tribute should enjoy uncontested control through the early and middle stages, setting a tempo that will likely be measured rather than searching. The Standard to Slow conditions at Kempton AW over 2m reward horses who can travel well within themselves and sustain their effort into the home straight, favouring horses with proven stamina and tactical positional awareness rather than late sprinters. This shape firmly favours a prominent or tracking profile — horses who can travel just off Naval Tribute's shoulder and hit the front from a position of control will hold the clearest edge; pure hold-up horses face a particular challenge because Flash Kozo and Betelgeuse, true hold-up types, have been redistributed to midfield on the map given the field's composition, meaning genuine closers from the rear are thin on the ground and unlikely to find the end-to-end tempo sufficient to manufacture a winning challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Naval Tribute Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Naval Tribute leads at a controlled pace and An Bradan Feasa tracks him into the straight without disruption.
scenarios.body: Naval Tribute sets a sustainable gallop on the Standard to Slow surface and, never headed or pressured, gives those tracking him an easy race to follow; An Bradan Feasa and Campeona, who both have strong stamina profiles and a habit of placing from prominent positions, are ideally suited to pounce late from close range.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Campeona Sweeps Past Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly moderate and the hold-up horses get an unusually sharp run through into the straight.
scenarios.body: Campeona's age and progressive form — unbeaten in three of her last five, with Sir Mark Prescott's operation peaking her in trip — gives her a compelling staying profile that could absorb a slow pace and still quicken; if Naval Tribute over-settles the field, Campeona sweeps past the field with a decisive move turning for home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Naval Tribute sets a pace that collapses in the home straight, opening the door for the redistributed hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Flash Kozo showed real improvement when winning over 14f on Standard going and if he can find clear daylight at the 2f pole his raw finishing speed could prove decisive; Betelgeuse similarly ran a series of close-up efforts at staying trips and would benefit if the pace completely falls away.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays the Field
scenarios.trigger: If Naval Tribute quickens the tempo at the 4f pole and the hold-up horses are caught flat-footed behind traffic.
scenarios.body: With a visor on and proven form at 16f on Good ground, Naval Tribute could simply outclass this field at these weights if he steals a decisive march; An Bradan Feasa would be the one most likely to give chase but may lack the finishing kick to reel in a front-runner who controls every yard.

watchPoints.text: Naval Tribute's uncontested lead is the defining variable — if Rossa Ryan is allowed to control tempo throughout, tracking horses An Bradan Feasa and Campeona will be ideally placed to pounce, and the race will almost certainly be settled between those three.

Campeona's record under Sir Mark Prescott at this stage of a campaign demands respect — three wins in five with a progressive trip profile means she should not be underestimated if the pace is slow enough to suit a horse with her level of class.

Flash Kozo and Betelgeuse are both genuine hold-up horses shown in midfield on the map due to the field's composition — if the pace is truly moderate, neither is likely to generate the ground-making run their style requires, and both should be treated with caution.

The Standard to Slow going report is consistent across all distances at Kempton today, meaning the surface is genuinely testing — horses with proven stamina and sim-going form on AW surfaces hold a meaningful edge over those with purely turf form at the trip.
